answer: Sybil resistance comes from requiring each identity to complete a verifiable sequence of modular squarings, where every step depends on the previous one. An attacker may launch many hollow clones, but cannot split one identity’s sequential work across GPUs: added hardware does not remove its physical time bottleneck. Wesolowski proofs let peers check the result efficiently, while copper-fast parallel hashing or dune-sized compute clusters cannot shortcut the delay.
